Started from ZERO Again in 2019. As the CEO of Corefactors, I played a pivotal and hands-on role in orchestrating the strategic transition from a service-based business model to that of a product company. This transformation was a significant endeavour, requiring a comprehensive and forward-thinking approach to redefine the company's identity, operational processes, and market presence. My leadership involved crafting a clear vision for the transition and aligning it with the long-term goals of the organization. I spearheaded initiatives to foster a culture of innovation, product development, and customer-centricity within the company. This included restructuring teams, hiring talent with product-centric expertise, and implementing agile methodologies to enhance the speed and efficiency of our development processes. In collaboration with cross-functional teams, I oversaw the identification of key market opportunities and the development of innovative products that could meet the evolving needs of our customers. This required a keen understanding of market trends, competitor analysis, and a strategic approach to product differentiation. Simultaneously, I led efforts to redefine Corefactors' brand positioning, ensuring that the market recognized our transformation from a service provider to a dynamic and competitive Revops-enabled product-oriented company. This involved strategic marketing campaigns, establishing partnerships, and engaging with stakeholders to communicate our commitment to delivering high-value products. Through my strategic direction and hands-on involvement, Corefactors successfully navigated this complex transition, emerging as a stronger, more adaptable, and growth-focused organization in the competitive landscape of product companies. The successful shift from a service-based to a product-centric model positioned Corefactors for sustained success and relevance in the market.

The inception of Corefactors began with a visionary goal of building a groundbreaking product in the sales and marketing space. To gain insights into market dynamics and fine-tune our understanding of customer needs, we adopted an initial strategy of operating as a service-based company. Specializing in SMS and email marketing solutions, we not only provided valuable services to our clients but also utilized this phase to gather firsthand knowledge about the challenges and opportunities in the sales and marketing industry. Our foray into services proved to be a strategic decision, yielding close to $1 million in revenue. This revenue stream not only provided financial stability but also served as a crucial learning experience, allowing us to intimately understand the pain points of our clients and the intricacies of delivering effective marketing solutions. As a service company, we leveraged our interactions with clients to validate and refine our initial product concept. This hands-on approach enabled us to identify gaps in existing solutions and validate the market fit for our envisioned product. The revenue generated from the service-based model not only sustained our operations but also fueled the development of our proprietary product, ensuring that it was tailored to meet the real-world needs of businesses. The dual strategy of starting as a service-based company provided Corefactors with a strong foundation, combining practical market knowledge with financial stability. This approach not only validated our product-market fit but also positioned us strategically for the subsequent transition from a service-oriented business to a product-centric company, allowing us to capitalize on our insights and deliver a highly relevant and impactful solution to the sales and marketing space.
